extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers (wartime public)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting of daily wartime news, policy statements, human-interest items and institutional announcements for a general newspaper audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postwar planning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Development of effective methods for organized international co-operation and for making political adjustments without resort to violence. 2. Finding a practicable way to reduce and control armaments. 3. Creation of an organization of an international court of justice. 4. Making of sound arrangements for stabilizing currencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as central items in postwar planning discussions; presented as practical mechanisms the republics (and potentially the United Nations) might employ to maintain peace in the postwar world.

rubrics_metrics.name: International trade as a foundation for peace
rubrics_metrics.description: "If goods can't cross national frontiers, armies will." — Security also 'depends upon increased freedom in foreign trade.' Lowered trade barriers and freedom from trade discriminations are 'essential parts of the only foundation upon which lasting peace can be built.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argued in testimony to Congress: economic openness and reduced trade discrimination are prerequisites for international security and lasting peace; economic isolation undermines international co-operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards to include in reciprocal trade agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Protective precautions designed to shield American business against dumping, discrimination, unfair practices, fluctuating currencies, sudden changes in duties and third-country imports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested as concrete legislative or treaty safeguards to accompany reciprocal-trade liberalization; recommended these be written into law to guide future negotiators and to protect domestic industry while pursuing broader trade freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigator training curriculum and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-flight schooling (about nine weeks) with heavy academic emphasis (including higher calculus—42 hours equated to a college year); advanced navigation school (about 18 weeks) covering pilotage, dead reckoning, celestial navigation (day and night), use of the circular slide rule ('navigator's wife'), calibration, and simulated flights ('grope') using actual night photos and instrument data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is academically intensive (more than half the schedule), includes increased radio training and instrument care, uses lifelike simulated raids with identification tasks, and aims for near‑perfection in navigation performance under combat conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigator selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Navigators are expected to be intellectually mature, strong students (an 'animated calculator with nerves of ice'), capable of complex computations under fire; selection favors younger men even if they have less formal education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification centers channel applicants into navigator, pilot and bombardier schools; many successful navigators lacked college but performed well; practical preference for youth because of training effectiveness in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: manifest essential oneness of cooperating churches
rubrics_metrics.description: To manifest the essential oneness of the cooperating churches in spirit and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as the first objective in the proposed constitution for a North American Council of Churches; forms a criterion for membership and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: continue and extend work of interdenominational agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: To carry on work of interdenominational agencies affiliated with the North American Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a constitutional objective for the proposed council—an operational mandate to sustain existing interdenominational programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: promote cooperation and develop local councils/chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: To promote cooperation among churches and further the development of [chapters/compirils] of churches in communities, States, provinces and larger territorial units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to foster organizational development at multiple territorial levels so churches can coordinate more effectively across North America.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee for Economic Development: postwar research agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Top problems for study: how to attain high employment and productivity; business incentives and the relation of taxation to these incentives; termination of war contracts; disposal of surplus stocks and Government‑financed plants; experience of the 1918–20 postwar period; removal of wartime controls; money and banking; changes in the tax structure; job migrations; unemployment prospects; agriculture; and international trade and finance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee staff directed to research these topics to stimulate postwar thinking among businessmen (not to plan for individual firms); findings intended to inform national economic planning within two years after the war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal for post-war international trusteeship with definite timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: Mme. Chiang proposed that a post-war world council led by the great powers exercise disinterested control (a transitional period of supervision) over countries that have not kept pace with world civilization, with the promise of a definite date for freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a pragmatic compromise between immediate independence and prolonged domination—supervision would be temporary, disinterested, and include a clear timetable for granting full freedom; the U.S. pre-war plan for the Philippines cited as an example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of leading nations to secure cooperation of less powerful members
rubrics_metrics.description: If the four great nations (United States, Great Britain, Russia and China) take the lead in forming such a plan, the less powerful members of the United Nations would cooperate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mme. Chiang argued that leadership by major powers would legitimize transitional arrangements and elicit cooperation from smaller nations in implementing postwar trusteeship or guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to release Nehru to gain India's cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mme. Chiang urged the release of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, asserting he should be freed to throw India’s political weight into the United Nations’ cause because he had a world vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a tactical/political recommendation: freeing a respected Indian leader would facilitate India's broader cooperation with Allied postwar objectives; contrasted with her view that Gandhi lacked a comparable world vision.
